name: VisionKit
summary: Identify and extract information in the environment using the device’s camera, or in images that your app displays.

declarations.name: DataScannerViewController
declarations.comment:
An object that scans the camera live video for text, data in text, and
machine-readable codes.

Use a `DataScannerViewController` object to get input from physical objects
that appear in the camera’s live video, such as printed text and QR codes on
packages.

Create a data scanner by passing parameters that configure the interface to
the
``DataScannerViewController/init(recognizedDataTypes:qualityLevel:recognizesMultipleItems:isHighFrameRateTrackingEnabled:isPinchToZoomEnabled:isGuidanceEnabled:isHighlightingEnabled:)``
initializer. Then set its delegate to an object in your app that implements
the ``DataScannerViewControllerDelegate`` protocol.

Before presenting the view controller, check whether the data scanner is
available using the ``DataScannerViewController/isSupported`` and
``DataScannerViewController/isAvailable`` properties. Before you can use the
data scanner, you must provide a reason for using the camera (add the
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/bundleresources/information_property_list/nscamerausagedescription>
key to the information property list), and a person must agree when the
system dialog first appears.

Then begin data scanning by invoking the
``DataScannerViewController/startScanning()`` method and implement the
``DataScannerViewControllerDelegate/dataScanner(_:didTapOn:)-4z7ql`` and
similar delegate methods to handle user actions. Use the ``RecognizedItem``
parameter passed to these methods to perform data-specific actions. For
example, if the item is a QR code, perform an action with its payload
string, such as opening a URL in a browser, or calling a phone number.

Alternatively, you can track items that appear in the live video using the
asynchronous ``DataScannerViewController/recognizedItems`` array.

members.name: init
members.signature: @MainActor init(recognizedDataTypes: Set<DataScannerViewController.RecognizedDataType>, qualityLevel: DataScannerViewController.QualityLevel = .balanced, recognizesMultipleItems: Bool = false, isHighFrameRateTrackingEnabled: Bool = true, isPinchToZoomEnabled: Bool = true, isGuidanceEnabled: Bool = true, isHighlightingEnabled: Bool = false)
members.comment:
Creates a scanner for finding data, such as text and machine-readable
codes, in the camera’s live video.

- Parameter recognizedDataTypes: The types of data that the data scanner
identifies in the live video.
- Parameter qualityLevel: The level of resolution to scan that depends on the size
of the items.
- Parameter recognizesMultipleItems: A Boolean value that indicates whether the
scanner identifies all items in the live video.
- Parameter isHighFrameRateTrackingEnabled: A Boolean value that determines the
frequency that the scanner updates the geometry of recognized items.
- Parameter isPinchToZoomEnabled: A Boolean value that indicates whether people can
use a two-finger pinch-to-zoom gesture.
- Parameter isGuidanceEnabled: A Boolean value that indicates whether the scanner
provides help to a person when selecting items.
- Parameter isHighlightingEnabled: A Boolean value that indicates whether the
scanner displays highlights around recognized items.

members.name: recognizedDataTypes
members.comment: The types of data that the data scanner identifies in the live video.

members.name: overlayContainerView
members.comment:
A view that the data scanner displays over its view without interfering
with the Live Text interface.

Optionally, add custom highlights to this view that doesn’t interfere
with hit-testing or the guidance objects. If you want to add interface
objects above the highlights, add those objects as subviews of the
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/uikit/uiviewcontroller/1621460-view>
property.

members.name: isScanning
members.comment:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the data scanner is actively looking
for items.

members.name: zoomFactor
members.comment:
The zoom factor for the live video in the camera.

Set this property to a value between the
``DataScannerViewController/minZoomFactor`` and
``DataScannerViewController/maxZoomFactor`` properties.

members.name: isAvailable
members.comment:
A Boolean value that indicates whether a person grants your app access
to the camera and doesn’t have any restrictions to using the camera.

For example, this property may be
`false` if a person
has Screen Time restrictions.

members.name: isSupported
members.comment:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the device supports data
scanning.

For this property to be
`true`, the device
must have the A12 Bionic chip or later. This property is `false` for apps running in visionOS.

- Important: If your app requires data scanning for its core functionality,
you can make your app available only on devices that support data scanning.
Add the
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/bundleresources/information_property_list/uirequireddevicecapabilities>
key to your app’s information property list and include the
`iphone-ipad-minimum-performance-a12` subkey in the array of device
capabilities.

members.name: capturePhoto
members.comment:
Captures a high-resolution photo of the camera’s live video.

- Returns: An image of the live video.

members.name: qualityLevel
members.comment:
The resolution that the scanner uses to find data.

The default value is
``DataScannerViewController/QualityLevel-swift.enum/balanced``. To
increase recognition speed for larger items, you can set this property
to ``DataScannerViewController/QualityLevel-swift.enum/fast``. For
smaller items, you can set this property to
``DataScannerViewController/QualityLevel-swift.enum/accurate`` but it
may impact the recognition speed.

members.name: stopScanning
members.comment:
Stops scanning the camera’s live video for data.

This method removes all items from the
``DataScannerViewController/recognizedItems`` property.

members.name: maxZoomFactor
members.comment: The maximum zoom factor that the camera supports.

members.name: minZoomFactor
members.comment: The minimum zoom factor that the camera supports.

members.name: startScanning
members.comment: Starts scanning the camera’s live video for data.

members.name: recognizedItems
members.comment:
An asynchronous array of items that the data scanner currently
recognizes in the camera’s live video.

You can use this property instead of the
``DataScannerViewControllerDelegate`` protocol methods to track the
recognized items in real time. To get the changes between arrays, use
the
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/swift/array/difference(from:)>
method. For more information on asynchronous streams, see
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/swift/concurrency>.

Text items in this array appear in the reading order of the language and
region.

members.name: regionOfInterest
members.comment:
The area of the live video in view coordinates that the data scanner
searches for items.

If you add interface objects to the live video (using the
``DataScannerViewController/overlayContainerView`` property) that might
hide items from a person, set this property to restrict the scanning
area. The default value is the bounds of the view.

members.name: isGuidanceEnabled
members.comment:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the scanner provides help to a
person when selecting items.

The guidance text, such as “Slow Down,” appears over the live video. The
default value for this property is
`true`.

members.name: isPinchToZoomEnabled
members.comment:
A Boolean value that indicates whether people can use a two-finger
pinch-to-zoom gesture.

The default value is
`true`.

members.name: isHighlightingEnabled
members.comment:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the scanner displays highlights
around recognized items.

The default value is
`false`.

members.name: recognizesMultipleItems
members.comment:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the scanner should identify all
items in the live video.

If `true`, the scanner
finds all items in the live video. If
`false`, the scanner
finds only the item closest to a person’s point of interest. The point
of interest is the middle of the view by default or where a person taps
in the live video. The default value is
`false`.

members.name: isHighFrameRateTrackingEnabled
members.comment:
A Boolean value that determines the frequency at which the scanner
updates the geometry of recognized items.

If `true`, the scanner
updates the geometry of items more frequently allowing your app to
closely track recognized items. If you don’t track items in the live
video, set this property to
`false`. The default
value is `true`.

members.name: supportedTextRecognitionLanguages
members.comment: The identifiers for the languages that the data scanner recognizes.

members.name: delegate
members.comment:
The delegate that handles user interaction with items recognized by the
data scanner.

The possible quality levels that the scanner uses to find data.

declarations.comment: A type of data that the scanner recognizes.

members.name: text
members.comment:
Creates a data type for text and information the scanner finds in
text.

Use this method to create a custom text data type. For example, if
you know the content contains languages other than a person’s
preferred languages, pass identifiers for those languages as the
`languages` parameter. If you only want to scan for telephone
numbers, pass
``DataScannerViewController/TextContentType/telephoneNumber`` as the
`textContentType` parameter.

To get the data scanner supported languages, use the
``DataScannerViewController/supportedTextRecognitionLanguages``
property.

- Parameter languages: The identifiers for the languages that you want
prioritized in the order of language processing. To specify a
person’s preferred languages, pass an empty set. This parameter gives the scanner
a hint on which language processing models to use. The scanner still recognizes all
supported languages.
- Parameter textContentType: The specific type of semantic text to find. To
identify all content types, pass `nil`.

- Returns: A text data type.

members.name: barcode
members.comment:
Creates a data type for barcodes the use the specified symbologies.

- Parameter symbologies: The barcode symbologies that the scanner recognizes.

- Returns: A barcode data type for the specified symbologies.

declarations.name: ImageAnalysis
declarations.comment:
An object that represents the results of analyzing an image, and provides
the input for the Live Text interface object.

An `ImageAnalysis` object represents the results of an ``ImageAnalyzer``
object finding items in an image that people can interact with. To create
an `ImageAnalysis` object, use the `ImageAnalyzer` class's
``ImageAnalyzer/analyze(_:configuration:)`` method variety, passing
the image and an ``ImageAnalyzer/Configuration`` object that specifies the
items you want to find. Then pass the image analysis to either an
``ImageAnalysisInteraction`` object for iOS or an ``ImageAnalysisOverlayView``
object for macOS to provide the Live Text interface.

members.name: hasResults
members.signature: final func hasResults(for analysisTypes: ImageAnalyzer.AnalysisTypes) -> Bool
members.comment:
Returns a Boolean value that indicates whether the analysis finds the
specified types in the image.

- Parameter analysisTypes: The data types you want to find in the image.

- Returns: `true` if the image analysis has results for the specified types; otherwise, `false`.

members.name: transcript
members.comment:
The string that the text items in the image represent.

The text appears in the reading order of the language and region.

declarations.name: ImageAnalysisInteraction
declarations.comment:
An interface that enables people to interact with recognized text, barcodes, and other objects in an image.

This class enables people to interact with specific content types (``ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes``) that the framework identifies in an image. For example:
- The Live Text interface enables them to select any text present in the image (``ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/textSelection``), or invoke a URL (``ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/dataDetectors``). The text selection UI offers framework-standard buttons for copying selected text, or looking it up on the web for more information.
- The *subject lift* feature identifies a wide variety of objects, or *subjects*, in images with the ``ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/imageSubject`` interaction type, and provides your app with an image of the objects with the background removed. The ``ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/visualLookUp`` type supplements this feature by adding a button in the bottom corner of the view that people can click or tap for more information about the recognized subjects.

## Configure the interface and begin interaction

This class conforms to the <doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/uikit/uiinteraction> protocol. To connect the interface with an image that your app displays, call <doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/uikit/uiview/2891013-addinteraction> on your app's image view and pass in a new instance of this class.

Choose the items that the framework recognizes in an image by configuring the  ``ImageAnalysisInteraction/preferredInteractionTypes`` property. To recognize all types of content, specify the ``ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/automatic`` option, or choose a combination of types by assigning an array:

```swift
interaction.preferredInteractionTypes = [.textSelection, .imageSubject]
```
To begin interaction, call one of the ``ImageAnalyzer`` class's `analyze` methods, such as ``ImageAnalyzer/analyze(_:configuration:)`` and set the result onto this class's ``ImageAnalysisOverlayView/analysis`` property.

You can take more control over the interaction or provide details about your app's image view by implementing a delegate (``ImageAnalysisInteractionDelegate``) and assigning it to the ``ImageAnalysisInteraction/delegate`` property. If your image view isn't an instance of <doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/uikit/uiimageview>, your app needs to define the interactive area within the image by implementing the ``ImageAnalysisInteractionDelegate/contentsRect(for:)-187x`` method.

members.name: view
members.signature: @MainActor @preconcurrency weak final var view: UIView? { get }
members.comment: The view that uses this interaction.

members.name: activeInteractionTypes
members.comment:
The types of interactions that a person actively performs.

This property is always a concrete type that’s never set to
``ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/automatic``.

members.name: preferredInteractionTypes
members.signature: @MainActor final var preferredInteractionTypes: ImageAnalysisInteraction.InteractionTypes { get set }
members.comment:
The types of interactions that people can perform with the image.

You need to set this property to enable interactions with the image. If
this property contains
``ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/automatic``, the interaction
ignores the other types in the set. The default value for this property
is an empty array that disables any interactions.

If you set this property to one or more types, the interaction sets the
view’s
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/uikit/uiview/1622577-isuserinteractionenabled>
property to `true` so
that the interaction begins. For example, when you’re ready to start the
Live Text interface, set this property to
``ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/automatic``.

If you set this property to an empty array, the image analysis
interaction doesn’t reset the view’s `isUserInteractionEnabled` property
to `false`.

members.name: contentsRect
members.comment:
A rectangle, in unit coordinate space, that describes the content area
of the interaction.

If the interaction’s view isn't an instance of
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/uikit/uiimageview>, your app sets the value for this property by implementing the ``VisionKit/ImageAnalysisInteractionDelegate`` callback ``VisionKit/ImageAnalysisInteractionDelegate/contentsRect(for:)-187x``. The
default return value is the unit rectangle, `[0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]`, which represents the whole view contents.

members.comment: The current selected text.

members.comment:
Returns a Boolean value that indicates whether the analysis finds text

text exists at `point`; otherwise,
`false`.

members.name: hasDataDetector

members.comment:
Returns a Boolean value that indicates whether the analysis detects data
at the specified point.

- Parameter point:  A point in the image, in view coordinates.

- Returns: `true` if
the analyzer detects data at `point`; otherwise,
`false`.

members.name: hasInteractiveItem
members.signature: @MainActor final func hasInteractiveItem(at point: CGPoint) -> Bool
members.comment:
Returns a Boolean value that indicates whether active text, data
detectors, or supplementary interface objects exist at the specified
point.

- Parameter point:  A point in the image, in view coordinates.

- Returns: `true` if
active text, data detectors, or supplementary interface objects exist at
`point`; otherwise,
`false`.

members.comment: Removes a person’s text selection from the interface.

members.comment: All highlighted subjects in the interaction image.

members.name: liveTextButtonVisible
members.comment:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the Live Text button appears.

When a person taps the Live Text button, it highlights recognized items
in the image.

members.name: hasActiveTextSelection
members.comment:
A Boolean value that indicates whether a person or the app has text selected within the image.

If ``VisionKit/ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/textSelection`` is an active
interaction type, a person can select text using a standard input method and the app can select text through the ``selectedRanges`` property.
If neither a person nor the app select any text, then this property returns `false`.

members.name: selectedAttributedText
members.comment: The current selected attributed text.

members.name: hasSupplementaryInterface
members.signature: @MainActor final func hasSupplementaryInterface(at point: CGPoint) -> Bool
members.comment:
Returns a Boolean value that indicates whether supplementary interface
objects exist at the specified point.

Supplementary interface objects include the Live Text button and Quick
Actions, depending on the item type.

- Parameter point: A point in the image, in view coordinates.

- Returns: `true` if
supplementary interface objects exist at `point`; otherwise,
`false`.

members.name: selectableItemsHighlighted
members.signature: @MainActor final var selectableItemsHighlighted: Bool { get set }
members.comment:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the interaction highlights
actionable text or data the analyzer detects in text.

The interaction object manages this property value for you. It sets this
property to `false` if
you set the ``ImageAnalysisInteraction/analysis`` property or the
``ImageAnalysisInteraction/activeInteractionTypes`` property to an empty
set. Otherwise, it sets this property depending on whether a person
toggles the Live Text button in the interface.

members.name: setContentsRectNeedsUpdate
members.comment:
Informs the view that contains the image when the layout changes and the
view needs to reload its content.

The framework ignores calls to this method when your app adds the interaction to a <doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/uikit/uiimageview>,
which calculates the ``contentsRect`` based on the image view's <doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/uikit/uiviewcontentmode>.

When the view that contains the image isn’t an instance of
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/uikit/uiimageview>, call this method when the layout changes. The interaction then invokes the delegate’s
``ImageAnalysisInteractionDelegate/contentsRect(for:)-187x`` callback, which provides the updated content area to the system.

members.name: supplementaryInterfaceFont
members.signature: @MainActor final var supplementaryInterfaceFont: UIFont? { get set }
members.comment:
The font to use for the supplementary interface.

The interaction also uses the font weight for image symbols, but ignores
the point size to keep button sizes consistent.

members.signature: @MainActor final var isSupplementaryInterfaceHidden: Bool { get set }

A Boolean value that indicates whether the view hides supplementary
interface objects.

Supplementary interface objects include the Live Text button and Quick
Actions, depending on the item type. Setting this property invokes the
``ImageAnalysisInteraction/setSupplementaryInterfaceHidden(_:animated:)``
method, passing this property value and
`true` for the
`animated` parameter.

members.name: setSupplementaryInterfaceHidden
members.signature: @MainActor final func setSupplementaryInterfaceHidden(_ hidden: Bool, animated: Bool)
members.comment:
Hides or shows supplementary interface objects, such as the Live Action
button and Quick Actions, depending on the item type.

- Parameter hidden: `true` to
hide the supplementary interface; otherwise,
`false`.
- Parameter animated: `true` to
animate the interface transition; otherwise,
`false`.

members.name: supplementaryInterfaceContentInsets

members.comment:
The distances the edges of content are inset from the supplementary
interface.

members.name: allowLongPressForDataDetectorsInTextMode
members.signature: @MainActor final var allowLongPressForDataDetectorsInTextMode: Bool { get set }
members.comment:
A Boolean value that indicates whether people can press and hold text to
activate data detectors.

If you set this property to
`true` when the
interaction type is just text, people can press and hold data in text,
even when data detectors aren’t active. Otherwise, people can perform
only text actions, such as copy and translate. The default value for
this property is
`true`.

members.name: visualLookUp
members.comment:
An option that presents a button for more information on any subjects the framework recognizes in the image.

When the framework identifies something familiar in an image that it can provide more information about (see ``ImageAnalysisInteraction/Subject``), it offers
a button in the bottom-right corner of the view. When people tap the button, a modal sheet appears that offers info about the subject.
For example, if the image contains a dog, the modal sheet describes the dog's breed and provides a relevant web URL where people can read more about the breed.

VisionKit supports Visual Look Up when it recognizes the following subjects:
- Plants and flowers
- Animals, such as cats, dogs, birds, reptiles, and insects
- Places, such as constructed landmarks, sculptures, and natural landmarks
- Art and media, such as paintings, books, and album covers
- Food, such as prepared dishes and desserts
- Symbols, such as laundry care labels and vehicle dashboard indicators

members.name: dataDetectors
members.comment:
An option that enables interaction with text of certain formats,
such as URLs, email addresses, and physical addresses.

People interact with *data detectors*, or UI that highlights each instance of
the recognized formats in text that's on an image. The data detectors appear without a Live Text button, because
people can't interact with other text with this option.

members.name: textSelection
members.comment:
An option that enables text selection, copying, and translating.

People can select text to perform actions. In this mode, the framework disables data detectors (``VisionKit/ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/dataDetectors``) by default. However, if you set the
``ImageAnalysisInteraction/allowLongPressForDataDetectorsInTextMode``
property to `true`, a person can use a long-press gesture to enable them.

members.name: automaticTextOnly
members.comment:
An option that enables all interaction types except image subjects and Visual Look Up.

This option represents the ``VisionKit/ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/automatic`` type, but excludes the ``VisionKit/ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/imageSubject`` and ``VisionKit/ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/visualLookUp`` types.

An option that enables interaction with any type of text, symbols, or subjects that the framework recognizes.

People can select text to perform actions, and after tapping the
Live Text button, they can interact with data detectors. If the
``ImageAnalysisInteraction/allowLongPressForDataDetectorsInTextMode``

declarations.name: ImageAnalysisInteraction.Subject
declarations.comment:
An area of interest in an image that the framework identifies as a primary focal point.

A *subject* is a foreground object in an image.
A single image can have multiple subjects. For example, in an image of three different coffee mugs, the framework may classify all three mugs as separate subjects.
In cases where the framework can't separate overlapping objects in a photo as individual subjects, a subject may consist of two or more objects.

VisionKit enables your app to extract, or *lift*, the image subjects individually, or together, with the background removed. For more information, see ``ImageAnalysisInteraction/Subject/image``.

An ``VisionKit/ImageAnalysisInteraction`` object contains an array of subjects (``VisionKit/ImageAnalysisInteraction/subjects``) that activates when ``ImageAnalysisInteraction/preferredInteractionTypes`` contains a subject-related option, such as ``ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/automatic``, or ``ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/imageSubject``.

Your app can also present a button that gives more information on an image's subjects by enabling the ``ImageAnalysisInteraction/InteractionTypes/visualLookUp`` interaction type.

declarations.name: ImageAnalyzer
declarations.comment:
An object that finds items in images that people can interact with, such
as subjects, text, and QR codes.

To use an `ImageAnalyzer` object, first create an
``ImageAnalyzer/Configuration`` object, and specify the types of items you
want to find in an image. Then pass the image you want to analyze and the
configuration object to an `ImageAnalyzer` object using the
``ImageAnalyzer/analyze(_:configuration:)`` or similar method. This method
returns an ``ImageAnalysis`` object that contains all the data VisionKit
needs to implement the Live Text interface.

Next, show the Live Text interface. For iOS apps, set the
interaction object of the view that contains the image to an instance of
``ImageAnalysisInteraction`` and set its
``ImageAnalysisInteraction/analysis`` property to the `ImageAnalysis`
object. To enable interactions with the image, set the interaction object’s
``ImageAnalysisInteraction/preferredInteractionTypes`` property. To
customize the Live Text interface, set the `ImageAnalysisInteraction
`object’s ``ImageAnalysisInteraction/delegate`` property and implement the
``ImageAnalysisInteractionDelegate`` protocol methods.

For macOS apps, add an `ImageAnalysisOverlayView` object above the view that
contains the image, and set its `analysis` property. To enable interactions
with the image, set the overlay view’s `preferredInteractionTypes` property.
Set the `ImageAnalysisOverlayView `object’s `delegate` property and
implement the `ImageAnalysisOverlayViewDelegate` protocol methods.

By default, the Live Text interface starts immediately when you show the
view.

members.name: isSupported
members.signature: final class var isSupported: Bool { get }
members.comment:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the device supports image analysis.

Check this property at runtime to determine if the device supports finding text, machine-readable codes, and subjects
in images. The system sets this property to `true` on devices that have an A12 Bionic chip or later.

For more information on the kinds of things the analyzer finds in images, see ``ImageAnalyzer/AnalysisTypes``.

- Note: If image analysis is a fundamental requirement for your app's operation,
you can prevent unsupported devices from installing your app. Add the
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/bundleresources/information_property_list/uirequireddevicecapabilities>
key to your app’s `Info.plist` (or update the key if it's already present) and include the array member
`iphone-ipad-minimum-performance-a12`.

members.name: visualLookUp
members.comment:
An option that analyzes an image for subjects that the framework can look up for more information.

When the framework recognizes a particular type of subject in an image, it offers
an interface for people to learn more about the subject. For example,
if an image contains a rose, the framework recognizes a plant and enables people to tap
the plant which presents a sheet with a list of additional resources on the specific type of plant —
in this case, a rose.

For more information about subjects in images, see ``ImageAnalysisInteraction/Subject``.

members.name: machineReadableCode
members.comment:
An option that analyzes an image for machine-readable codes, such as QR codes.

The framework recognizes the following code types:

Aztec, Codebar, Code 39 Checksum,
Code 39, Code 39 Full ASCII, Code 39 Full ASCII Checksum,
Code 93, Code 93, Code 128, Matrix EAN-8, Data,
EAN-13, GS1 DataBar Expanded, GS1 DataBar Limited, ITF,
ITF-14, MicroPDF417, MicroQR, PDF417 QR, UPC-E

- Important: The framework ignores this option on macOS.
